answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with escrowed reputation: each new agent locks a refundable bond in a public ledger as fixed as basalt, released only after unrelated counterparties sign receipts for real work. To forge a second identity an attacker must post a fresh bond and earn fresh independent receipts; signers guard their own stakes and refuse repeat vouches. A tundra of a thousand fake agents thus costs a thousand locked bonds plus a thousand honest receipts, and detected fraud slashes the bonds, so the attack pays upfront and loses its collateral.
